# Governing equation

The equations are expressed in the general orthogonal coordinate system:

```math
\frac{1}{{J}} \frac{\partial}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} \left( \frac{{J}}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} {{u}_{{j}}} \right) = 0,
```

```math
\frac{\partial {{u}_{{i}}}}{\partial {t}} = - \frac{{{u}_{{j}}}}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} \frac{\partial {{u}_{{i}}}}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} - \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{i}}}}}} \frac{\partial {p}}{\partial {{\xi}^{{i}}}} + \frac{1}{{Re}} \frac{1}{{J}} \frac{\partial}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} \left( \frac{{J}}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} \frac{\partial {{u}_{{i}}}}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} \right),
```

where ${{h}_{{{\xi}^{{i}}}}}$ is the scale factor:

```math
\frac{\partial {{x}_{{i}}}}{\partial {{\xi}^{{i}}}},
```

and ${J}$ is the Jacobian determinant defined as:

```math
{\prod_{{i}} {{h}_{{{\xi}^{{i}}}}}}.
```

Note that summation is taken with respect to ${j}$.
See [the other documentation](https://naokihori.github.io/SimpleTCSolver/index.html) for details.

The equations are integrated by means of the predictor-corrector approach: the velocity field is predicted:

```math
{{{u}_{{i}}}^{{*}}} = {{{u}_{{i}}}^{{n}}} + {\int_{{{t}^{{n}}}}^{{{t}^{{n + 1}}}} {{(RHS)}_{{i}}} d{t}},
```

which is corrected to enforce the incompressibility:

```math
{{{u}_{{i}}}^{{n + 1}}} = {{{u}_{{i}}}^{{*}}} - {\int_{{{t}^{{n}}}}^{{{t}^{{n + 1}}}} \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{i}}}}}} \frac{\partial {\psi}}{\partial {{\xi}^{{i}}}} d{t}},
```

where ${\psi}$ is scalar field obtained by solving the Poisson equation:

```math
{\int_{{{t}^{{n}}}}^{{{t}^{{n + 1}}}} \frac{1}{{J}} \frac{\partial}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} \left( \frac{{J}}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} \frac{\partial {\psi}}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} \right) d{t}} = \frac{1}{{J}} \frac{\partial}{\partial {{\xi}^{{j}}}} \left( \frac{{J}}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{{j}}}}}} {{{u}_{{j}}}^{{*}}} \right).
```

Now, we consider this equation explicitly in a two-dimensional Cartesian coordinates.
Since each scale factor ${{h}_{{{\xi}^{{i}}}}}$ is a function of the coordinate in the corresponding direction ${{x}_{{i}}}$, or in other words since the scale factor in the first direction is independent in the second direction (and vice versa), the Poisson equation can be simplified as:

```math
{\int_{{{t}^{{n}}}}^{{{t}^{{n + 1}}}} \left( \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{1}}}}} \frac{\partial}{\partial {{\xi}^{1}}} \left( \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{1}}}}} \frac{\partial {\psi}}{\partial {{\xi}^{1}}} \right) + \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{2}}}}} \frac{\partial}{\partial {{\xi}^{2}}} \left( \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{2}}}}} \frac{\partial {\psi}}{\partial {{\xi}^{2}}} \right) \right) d{t}} = \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{1}}}}} \frac{\partial {{{u}_{1}}^{{*}}}}{\partial {{\xi}^{1}}} + \frac{1}{{{h}_{{{\xi}^{2}}}}} \frac{\partial {{{u}_{2}}^{{*}}}}{\partial {{\xi}^{2}}}.
```
